clue.text: Everywhere bar London loses from this tax?

definitions.text: Everywhere bar London loses from this tax?

parts.words: Everywhere bar London loses from this tax?
parts.note: read as a joke about regional inequality: if every place except the seat of government loses out, the chief city is the winner, and a levy on investment profits has that very name

explanation.surface: A grumble that some levy drains every region except London.
explanation.walkthrough: London is Britain's capital, so a tax where only London does well is read as one where the capital gains.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the levy charged on the profit made when an asset is sold for more than it cost.

clue.text: University cutting luxurious lawn

parts.note: Camb. is the abbreviation for Cambridge, the university

indicators.note: cutting means trimming the end off the word that follows

parts.note: rich means luxurious

explanation.surface: A college mowing its splendid grass.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cutting' drops the H from RICH, leaving RIC. Lawn here is the fine linen fabric, not grass.
explanation.definitionFit: Cambric and lawn are both fine, thin linen or cotton fabrics, so one stands for the other.

clue.text: Feeble-sounding security, admitting intruder from here?

indicators.note: the hyphenated sounding attached to feeble says only that word is spoken, so its spelling changes

parts.note: feeble means poor, which said aloud matches the first syllable of the place
a lock provides security

explanation.surface: A weak lock lets a burglar in.
explanation.walkthrough: Coleridge said his poem Kubla Khan was cut short by 'a person on business from Porlock', the most famous intruder in English literature.
explanation.definitionFit: Porlock is the Somerset village whose visitor interrupted Coleridge writing Kubla Khan, so an intruder came from there.

clue.text: Fund manager, often an Hon.

parts.note: the official who looks after a club's money, a post often held unpaid and so given the title Honorary, abbreviated Hon., which here pretends to be the courtesy title the Honourable

explanation.surface: Money people are often aristocrats.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hon.' looks like the Honourable, a title for a peer's child, but here it is Honorary, the unpaid office.
explanation.definitionFit: The officer of a society who manages its funds holds this post, often in an honorary capacity.

clue.text: Very modest contract: leading with a king makes good sense

indicators.note: leading with says the king's name comes in front of the contract

parts.note: King Log is the useless ruler in Aesop's fable of the frogs who asked for a king
in bridge, one club, written 1C and read as IC, is the lowest possible bid

explanation.surface: A bridge player's reasoning: bid low and lead the king.
explanation.walkthrough: The bridge contract is one club, IC; 'leading with' puts LOG first. The definition is a verb phrase standing for a noun, read as 'logic' being what makes good sense.
explanation.definitionFit: Logic is sound reasoning, the quality of an argument that makes good sense.

clue.text: Plane staff expressed satisfaction with the wind

parts.note: air is moving wind
crew is an old past tense of crow, to boast or exult, as in 'the cock crew'

explanation.surface: Cabin crew were pleased with the breeze.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Crew' as a past tense of crow (the cock crew) is old-fashioned but still in dictionaries.
explanation.definitionFit: The aircrew are the people who work on board an aeroplane, its staff.

clue.text: Start to nag when row becomes more unpleasant

indicators.note: the start of a word is its first letter

parts.note: as can mean when
a tier is a row, as of seats

explanation.surface: Nagging that turns into an argument makes things worse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'row' looks like a quarrel, but it is a line of seats.
explanation.definitionFit: Nastier is the comparative of nasty, meaning more unpleasant.

clue.text: European peoples forming a traditional PARE buffer

annotationWithheld.why: Clue held as 'European peoples forming a traditional PARE buffer': FRENCH + POLISH is clear but the definition is garbled by OCR ('PARE'), the scan is blank and no search gave the printed text.
annotationWithheld.clue: European peoples forming a traditional PARE buffer

clue.text: Guilty conscience about mouthful not finished

parts.note: re is Latin-derived crossword shorthand for about or concerning

indicators.note: something not finished lacks its final part, so the last letter is dropped

parts.note: a morsel is a small mouthful of food

explanation.surface: Feeling guilty about a bite of food left uneaten.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not finished' cuts the L from MORSEL, leaving MORSE.
explanation.definitionFit: Remorse is deep regret for a wrong done, the feeling of a guilty conscience.

clue.text: Jewel of a lass when love is involved

indicators.note: something involved is wrapped up inside, so these letters go within the word for lass

parts.note: a lass is a girl
as can mean when, as in 'as I left'
love is nil in tennis scoring, written O

explanation.surface: A gem belonging to a young woman once romance enters the picture.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is involved' sets two pieces into the lass word; 'when' standing for AS is the usual trap, since it reads as a mere link.
explanation.definitionFit: A girasol is a fire opal, a gemstone showing a red glow.

clue.text: Abandoned candidature, being too far behind

parts.note: left means abandoned
standing for office is being a candidate, so standing is candidature

explanation.surface: A dropped election bid left a candidate trailing.
explanation.definitionFit: To be left standing is to be completely outpaced, far behind the rest.

clue.text: Common sense keeps king very uneasy

indicators.note: to keep something is to hold it inside, so the sense word contains the other letters

parts.note: nous is everyday common sense
ER stands for Edwardus Rex, the royal cipher of King Edward

explanation.surface: Even a level head finds a monarch deeply unsettling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'keeps' holds the monarch's cipher and the abbreviation for very inside the word for common sense.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone nervous is anxious and on edge, which is to say uneasy.

clue.text: Capital, the way one gets into an eating place

indicators.note: to get into is to enter, so these letters go inside the café word

parts.note: a caff is British slang for a cheap café
RD is the abbreviation for road, a way
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Directions to a café: follow the road and you'll arrive.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gets into' places the road abbreviation and the numeral inside the eating-place word. A caff is a cheap, no-frills British café.
explanation.definitionFit: Cardiff is the capital city of Wales.

clue.text: Sign above letter? It makes a heck of a difference

definitions.text: Sign above letter? It makes a heck of a difference

parts.words: Sign above letter? It makes a heck of a difference
parts.note: an accent mark put over a letter changes its sound, and this mark's name looks like the exclamation heck with an extra letter

explanation.surface: A remark that a little accent mark changes a great deal.
explanation.walkthrough: The haček is the small v-shaped mark used in Czech over letters such as c and s; its name looks like 'heck' with an A put in.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the name of the inverted circumflex placed over a letter to change its sound in Czech and other Slavonic languages.

clue.text: Highway deeds holding up travellers

parts.note: a highway is a road
works are deeds, as in good works

explanation.surface: Highway robbery: crimes that stop people on their journeys.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests highwaymen holding up coaches; the definition means repairs that delay drivers.
explanation.definitionFit: Road repairs are what typically cause delays for motorists, so the definition describes them by their effect.

clue.text: The boy with 'er can't compare with the British Grenadier

definitions.text: can't compare with the British Grenadier

parts.note: Alex is a boy's name
and means with
the dropped-aitch form of her stands for ER, the Queen's royal cipher

explanation.surface: A lad and his girlfriend are no match for a grenadier.
explanation.walkthrough: The marching song The British Grenadiers begins 'Some talk of Alexander, and some of Hercules ... but none can compare with the British Grenadier'.
explanation.definitionFit: In the song, Alexander the Great is one of the heroes said to be no match for the British Grenadier.

clue.text: Subcontract? It sounds like a striking beginning

parts.note: workers who are striking are out
a source is a beginning or origin

explanation.surface: A firm notices that farming out work sounds like the start of a walkout.
explanation.walkthrough: 'It sounds like' only says the answer splits into two words; there is no soundalike here.
explanation.definitionFit: To outsource work is to contract it out to another firm, which is subcontracting it.

clue.text: Disorder in the Capitol is newsworthy

indicators.note: disorder means the letters of the following word are jumbled

explanation.surface: A riot at the US Capitol makes the headlines.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Disorder in' rearranges CAPITOL; 'the' and 'is' are link words.
explanation.definitionFit: Topical means relating to current events, and so newsworthy.

clue.text: Fundamental sort of farming

definitions.meaning: basic or inherent to the structure of something
farming without artificial fertilisers or pesticides, using only natural methods

explanation.definitionFit: Organic means inherent to a thing's structure, and also describes chemical-free farming.

clue.text: Scottish town where everyone has only half-helping of porridge?

parts.note: all means everyone

indicators.note: a half helping takes only part of the dish, here the first half of the word for porridge

parts.note: porridge is made from oats

explanation.surface: A Scottish town where everybody gets a meagre bowl of porridge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'half-helping of' takes OA, the first half of OATS.
explanation.definitionFit: Alloa is a town in central Scotland, on the River Forth.

clue.text: Worker is a new supporter of culture

indicators.note: in a down clue a supporter sits underneath, so these letters come after the culture word

parts.note: art is culture

explanation.surface: A craftsman is a fresh patron of the arts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'supporter of' puts ISAN below ART in the down light.
explanation.definitionFit: An artisan is a skilled manual worker, a craftsman.

clue.text: Big ship, the Bounty

parts.note: large means big
SS is the abbreviation for steamship

explanation.surface: A large vessel, HMS Bounty.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface points to HMS Bounty of the famous mutiny; 'bounty' here means generosity.
explanation.definitionFit: Largess is generous giving, and bounty means generosity, so they are synonyms.

clue.text: Criticises marks in Pugin's building

indicators.note: M is placed inside the rearranged letters
building means putting together anew, so the letters of the name are reassembled

parts.note: the name Pugin with its possessive s, used as letters
M is the abbreviation for marks, the old German currency

explanation.surface: Someone finds fault with the marks on a building by the architect Pugin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'building' rearranges PUGINS to IPUGNS, and 'in' puts M inside it after the I. A.W.N. Pugin was the Victorian Gothic architect.
explanation.definitionFit: To impugn something is to challenge or attack it, so impugns means criticises.

clue.text: They make it difficult to see in a dusty escritoire

definitions.text: They make it difficult to see

indicators.note: the answer sits inside the run of letters of the words that follow

explanation.surface: Things obscuring the view in a dusty writing desk.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters run across 'duSTY ESCritoire'.
explanation.definitionFit: Styes are inflamed swellings on the eyelid, which make it hard to see.

clue.text: A time spent getting dressed

parts.note: spent means exhausted, tired

explanation.surface: Getting ready to go out takes a while.
explanation.definitionFit: Attired means clothed, which is the same as dressed.

clue.text: Cut back money for London borough

parts.note: to hack is to cut roughly

indicators.note: back says the money word is read from right to left

parts.note: the yen is the Japanese currency

explanation.surface: A council slashes its budget.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns YEN into NEY. Hackney is a borough in north-east London.
explanation.definitionFit: Hackney is one of the boroughs making up Greater London.

clue.text: See Cinders in transformation scene

indicators.note: a transformation changes the shape of the letters, like the pantomime scene where Cinderella's rags become a gown

explanation.surface: Watch Cinderella's change at the pantomime.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in transformation scene' rearranges CINDERS into the answer. In British pantomime the transformation scene is where Cinderella is magically dressed for the ball.
explanation.definitionFit: To discern something is to perceive or make it out, which is to see it.

clue.text: Girl pops up somewhere in the outback

parts.note: Alice is a girl's name
springs means appears suddenly, pops up

explanation.surface: A young woman appears suddenly in the Australian bush.
explanation.definitionFit: Alice Springs is a town in the middle of Australia's Northern Territory, deep in the outback.
